messages:
cheng: quick ping — after today's vectorizer chart bump some staging pods started failing to decrypt secrets (KMS). helm upgrade + rollout seemed fine but workloads throw `AccessDeniedException` on decrypt. anyone seen this pattern with IRSA+kms grants recently?
maria: ugh. do you have the SA annotation and the role binding still applied? sometimes helm hooks re-create the SA with a different uid and annotation gets lost.
cheng: SA annotation exists: `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/vectorizer-irsa-role` on the serviceaccount. terraform shows `aws_kms_grant` in place too. snippet: ```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "vectorizer" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.vectorizer.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.vectorizer_irsa_role.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "Encrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
}
```
ryan: couple quick checks: 1) confirm the role ARN in SA is identical to tf role ARN (no extra path) 2) ensure key policy isn't constraining to `aws:PrincipalArn` that excludes `sts:assumed-role/*` 3) check audit logs for the exact principal in the failed decrypt (it will be an assumed-role ARN).
cheng: I checked CloudTrail — the principal on the failure is `arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/vectorizer-irsa-role:bootstrap` (note the session name). KMS error says `Not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt`.
james: interesting — KMS grants should allow that assumed-role principal if grantee_principal was the role ARN. But if the key policy has an explicit condition like `StringEquals: { "aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/vectorizer-irsa-role" }` it will fail because the actual principal is the assumed-role ARN.
maria: yep. our old pattern was to avoid PrincipalArn conditions and instead allow the IAM role in key policy or allow `arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/*` in the key policy. another approach is to grant to the role's ARN via `aws_kms_grant` (which creates a grant ARN that references the role) — but that still hits key policy conditions.
ryan: if you prefer minimal TF change: remove any `PrincipalArn` equality condition from the key policy and add a policy statement like: ```json
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/vectorizer-irsa-role" },
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
cheng: quick question — our terraform currently manages the key policy in a single `aws_kms_key.key_policy` JSON string. if I change the condition there, do I need to re-create grants?
james: no, grants remain. but be careful: if tf replaces the key (rare) grants are orphaned. changing policy is fine.
maria: also check the service that creates the KMS grant — if your pipeline creates grants on deploy, ensure it runs after TF ensures the role exists. race between role creation and grant creation is a common flake.
cheng: ok — I found a tiny ordering race in our deploy: helm chart creates SA simultaneously while TF applies role & grant in separate pipeline. that could explain intermittent failures. I'll reorder so TF role+grant apply first, then helm.
ryan: sounds good. another defensive option is to make the grant target the assumed-role principal pattern in the key policy, e.g., "AWS": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/vectorizer-irsa-role/*" — but that is less tidy.
maria: +1 to ordering. also add a quick smoke job after deploy that runs `aws kms decrypt` via the pod to confirm. saves paging.
cheng: thanks — I'll open a tiny PR to adjust the pipeline order and relax the PrincipalArn condition in the key policy. pinging @james for quick review.
james: on it. also update infra runbook note about the race and the CloudTrail check command: ```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --max-results 5
```
cheng: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/512 — includes TF key policy tweak + pipeline job re-order, and adds smoke job.
maria: skimming now. looks fine to me.
deploy-bot: CI pipeline started for infra PR #512 — plan in progress (plan id: plan-9832).
ryan: quick nit: in the key policy patch, please avoid hardcoding account id — use data.aws_caller_identity if possible.
cheng: will update. thanks all, will merge once CI green and tests pass. closing the loop here. :thumbsup:
